trigger_c.wall_clock_at_read: 07:10 -- 6 min after the close that produced it, so STALE in fact
trigger_c.why_not: Two independent refusals: (1) the premarket book was 0.84-0.93% wide at 07:02-07:06, over the 0.5% cap, so the entry would have been spread-vetoed at arming regardless; (2) the read happened 6 minutes after the 07:04 close because the cycle (delegated scan + batched bars + rank) takes ~4 min -- the tag's own 2-min freshness window had lapsed at wall-clock time even though the --as-of run stamped it fresh. The `trigger` command's own WARNING line ('as-of 07:06 vs wall clock 07:10 -- tags may be stale') caught this. Rule applied: never enter on a signal whose freshness is only nominal.
trigger_c.also: bullish_engulfing at the 07:00 close, already STALE at the 07:06 as-of.

trigger_c.why_not: Spread 1.25% at 07:21 (2.5x cap) -- vetoed at arming regardless. And the read lag (delegated scan + batched bars + rank = ~3 min) again exceeded the 2-min freshness window at wall-clock time. Premarket Trigger C on a spread-vetoed name is structurally untakeable; the 1-minute single-name poll is reserved for after 09:30 when the book can pass.

trigger_c.tag_at_read_0745: TAKEABLE NOW (1m since close) -- genuinely fresh at 07:45:19 wall clock
trigger_c.why_not: OPS DEFECT (self-inflicted, logged as an error): the cycle command chained `wait_until 07:47` AFTER the trigger call in the same tool call, so the TAKEABLE tag printed at 07:45:19 was not READ until 07:47:00 -- 4 min after the 07:43 close, outside the 2-min freshness window. This is exactly the Day-13 loop-ordering defect (2026-08-21) recurring: 'the read is the time-critical step; the wait is never allowed between the trigger call and reading its output'. Not entered: a stale tag is a refusal by rule, not by judgement. GTLB was otherwise armable at the moment (spread 0.31% at 07:38, halal PASS, calm, rank 1).
trigger_c.fix: from this point every cycle is bars -> cyc.py (read) as one step and the pacing wait as a SEPARATE later tool call.
